atlas.mapping: Picture a filing cabinet. Each table is a drawer. A row is one fact, and a shared tag such as the chip's name or the job's name is how a fact in one drawer is laid next to a fact in another. In a real hall the drawers would be filled by different systems: an inventory database for buildings and chips, a telemetry stream for temperature and power, a job scheduler for the race, and a storage system for saves. This rehearsal fills those same drawers with synthetic rows. The join is the same idea: chip name plus the step, or job name plus the step. Readings that belong to chips outside the job are not given a personal chart. Those chips are counted in the hall total.

decision_columns.name: gpu_temp_c
decision_columns.impact: A rule that looks only at temperature can bench a healthy busy chip. The better rules compare the temperature with the power.

decision_columns.name: power_draw_w
decision_columns.purpose: How much electrical power the chip is using.
decision_columns.impact: If temperature and power rise together, the page treats it as a busy spell and leaves the chip in the job.

decision_columns.name: power_limit_w
decision_columns.impact: Several chips on one feed dropping under the cap together become one incident. Chips on another feed stay out of it.

decision_columns.name: sm_util_ratio
decision_columns.purpose: How busy the chip's math engines are. The learned helper calls this util.
decision_columns.impact: Including it tells a busy chip from an idle one. The helper was scored with it and did not beat the simple rule, so the live rules stay in charge.

decision_columns.name: residual_ewma
decision_columns.purpose: How much hotter the chip is than expected for the power it is using, smoothed over recent steps.
decision_columns.impact: A high value, with a fresh reading and an aging save, asks for an extra save before the chip stops.

decision_columns.name: freshness_steps
decision_columns.purpose: How many steps have passed since the newest reading actually arrived.
decision_columns.impact: If this is too large, the page says the sensors are late and refuses to name a cause.

decision_columns.name: support_count
decision_columns.purpose: How many readings are in hand at decision time.
decision_columns.impact: Too few readings and the page refuses to guess, the way a doctor refuses a diagnosis from one old thermometer.

decision_columns.name: data_quality_ok
decision_columns.purpose: A yes or no that combines freshness and how many readings exist.
decision_columns.impact: When this is no, a preventive shutdown is blocked.

decision_columns.name: workload_temp_tracks_power
decision_columns.purpose: Whether the heat followed the power, which is what a healthy busy spell looks like.
decision_columns.impact: When this is yes, the page does not take an extra save just because the chip is warm.

decision_columns.name: checkpoint_age_steps
decision_columns.purpose: How many steps have passed since the last complete save.
decision_columns.impact: An old save plus a real heat warning asks for a new save. A brand-new complete save does not.

decision_columns.name: state
decision_columns.purpose: Whether a save is complete, still being written, or refused.
decision_columns.impact: Including it stops the page from reopening a half-finished save. Only a verified usable save can restart the job.

decision_columns.name: shards_present
decision_columns.purpose: How many pieces of the save arrived.
decision_columns.impact: Compared with shards_expected, a short count means the save is torn and is refused.

decision_columns.name: heartbeat_age_s
decision_columns.purpose: How long since a seat in the job last answered.
decision_columns.impact: A missing heartbeat can restart the job from the last complete save. It does not invent a heat warning.

decision_columns.name: capability
decision_columns.purpose: Whether this job may drop one chip or must restart as a choir.
decision_columns.impact: If the job is strict, a request to drop one singer is refused and the group restarts together.

decision_columns.name: power_limit_ratio
decision_columns.purpose: Power cap divided by the chip's normal full power. Used only on the learned helper's score sheet.
decision_columns.impact: Including it in the helper did not beat the simple heat rule, so it does not replace the live rules.

atlas.decision_plain: Hundreds of columns can be joined. Only this short list is allowed to change a reaction: save, restart, leave the chip alone, bench it, or refuse to guess. Including one of these can change that choice. Including a column that is not on this list adds context or a paper trail, and the live rules do not restart a job because of it. The learned helper was scored on five of these numbers and did not beat the simple rule, so the simple rule stays in charge.
